title: The claim heap, XMS and on-demand modules
summary: The heap's core model is the best-argued subsystem in the kernel: an out-of-band record table that is the allocator, two-ended placement, purgeability encoded in the owner word at zero record cost, relocation by callback through the holder's own dispatcher (no handle double-indirection on an 8088), one walk body for plan and run, and mem_avail defined as the question mem_claim answers. The weaknesses are at the edges: interrupt latency (mem_regrow copies at IF=0; mem_avail walks O(n^2) at IF=0), failure policy (a doomed claim sheds every cache and can park once per shed), a per-owner cap that also binds the kernel's shared tags (MEM_K_DRV: at most eight driver images), a purge floor any teardown lifts (a multi-file paste can silently stop part-way), the KB-shift carry surviving in the DMA head door, and a self-region widening that lets a package free or regrow the region it runs in (a documented choice in loader.inc, and one mem_owner_of_x depends on). Modules are solid (build + layout stamps, bounded entries, build-time-proven mod_cfix); the open risk is a worker-side drop freeing code the UI task is executing. xmem.inc is a clean overlay shim with three stale sentences. Most doc drift sits in orphaned headers of inlined routines and in SPEC 66.3, which still describes the MC_DMA-pins / no-park design.

strengths.title: The record IS the allocator, out of band
strengths.why: Free is one word store, no free list can disagree with the map, and the map is in .lowbss behind ss: so a package overrun cannot corrupt it (DOS's in-band MCBs can be killed by a one-byte overrun).

strengths.title: Purgeable class encoded in the owner word, priority in its high byte
strengths.why: Zero bytes per record, no notification protocol (zeroing the one naming word is the notice), and a rank-bounded cheapest-first shed so a cache can never evict a dearer one.

strengths.title: Relocation by callback rather than handles, default PINNED
strengths.why: Normal access is a plain segment load; only a move pays, once, through PKG_DISP so nobody writes a retf; MC_RLOC reset on every publish makes stale procs impossible. Cheaper per access than Mac handles or GEOS lock/unlock.

strengths.title: Plan and run are one body, direction is a mask
strengths.why: The plan cannot promise a run the moves do not deliver, by construction; complementing the key folds both passes into one scan.

strengths.title: The kernel's half is a table, and the IVT lesson is kept
strengths.why: A holder costs a 4-byte row; one loop, called once per address space (.bss, .lowbss, the IVT), covers them all; only IRQ vectors + int 33h are rewritten because unused IVT slots are scratch (tests/hdmove.py).

strengths.title: mem_avail answers mem_claim's question
strengths.why: The figure packages size down from models the compaction + shed a claim would really do, on both kernels; the under-report-is-invisible argument is written down.

strengths.title: DMA page rule as a monotonic bump inside the scan, preserved across moves
strengths.why: No claim-test-retry while holding blocks; regrow and both compaction passes keep the property a claim was granted under.

strengths.title: Module loader: two stamps, bounded entries, mod_gone, drop gate, proven cfix scan
strengths.why: A stale or hostile image is refused, not executed; unloaded slots refuse rather than jump; t_moddrop gates 'every module has a drop'; mod_cfix is a byte scan made safe by a build-time proof in tools/os88rom.py.

strengths.title: XMS as an overlay with one gate written last
strengths.why: No resident cost on an 8088, and the tier-0 refusals are byte-identical to what every package has already met on the target machine.

findings.title: MEM_OWNER_MAX caps the kernel's shared tags: the ninth driver image is refused with the heap free
findings.detail: mem_claim_1 counts every live record whose MC_OWN equals BX and refuses at MEM_OWNER_MAX (8) regardless of BX. Every driver image and every DRVC_OVL image loaded through drv_load_at (XMEM.DRV, SAVER.DRV, THMPAL.DRV) is claimed under the single tag MEM_K_DRV, and kern_big has DRV_MAX = 9 + DRV_VX + DRV_PX rows (SOUND, HDD, NET/ETHER, RAMDISK, VESA, EMS, CDROM, HTTPFS, USBMOUSE, PCIETHER). On a well-equipped AT (or where HMA_DRV declines) the ninth MEM_K_DRV claim fails exactly as 'no heap'. MEM_K_MOD and MEM_K_IMG share one owner each the same way. The cap's purpose is to charge an app that floods the table; it has no meaning for kernel tags whose counts the kernel bounds.
evidence: kernel/memory.inc:1095-1112 owner walk counts any BX
findings.recommendation: Skip the cap when BH = 0xFF (kernel tags); purgeable ranges are already per-ordinal owners. Add a gate that loads every driver on an AT profile, or an assembly-time check that the kernel tags' maxima fit MEM_MAX.
findings.verify_note: mem_claim_1's owner walk (memory.inc:1094-1112) counts MC_OWN == BX with no exception for BH = 0xFF, and every driver image is claimed as MEM_K_DRV (driver.inc:3513). HMA_DRV is only defined on ROM_COLD kern_big (kernel.asm:1166-1175), so a standard kern_big puts every image on the heap. Not listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST/KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE. Reaching nine needs XMEM.DRV plus eight drivers loaded at once, so it is latent on most profiles (the reviewer's open question 1).

findings.title: mem_regrow runs path 3's whole copy with interrupts off
findings.detail: mem_regrow is one pushf/cli window from entry to exit, and path 3 inside it runs mem_hifit (O(MEM_MAX^2)) and mem_bcopy of the whole old block. At ~25 clocks a word on a 4.77 MHz 8088 a 64KB canvas grow is ~170 ms at IF=0: ~20 serial-mouse bytes overrun the one-byte 8250 buffer, SB half-buffer IRQs are late, and two BIOS ticks are lost (the PIC holds one). The compactor solved the identical problem with [sch_lock] and IF=1; regrow is the outlier.
evidence: kernel/memory.inc:4664 popf only at the end
kernel/memory.inc:4040 mem_compact uses inc byte [sch_lock] instead
findings.recommendation: Decide the destination and publish under cli, raise [sch_lock], restore IF and copy, then cli only for the record store. Nobody can claim while switching is paused and ISRs do not claim.
findings.verify_note: mem_regrow's pushf/cli (memory.inc:4559-4560) brackets mem_hifit and mem_bcopy (4616, 4640) to the popf at the end; mem_bcopy itself never re-enables. The compactor raises [sch_lock] instead (mem_compact).

findings.title: A doomed claim sheds every cache and may park workers once per shed
findings.detail: kern_big's retry loop is compact -> shed one -> retry until nothing is left to shed; mem_compact clears [mem_parked] at .end so each call may park again (INST_PARKW = 4 ticks). A claim bigger than the whole heap destroys MEM_P_DIRW (priced 'seconds') and the FAT windows before CF=1. A real caller probes this way: cmz_wclaim tries the largest window first and halves on refusal, so the first refusal has already shed everything before a window that fits without shedding is tried.
findings.recommendation: (a) Before the first compaction compare the request with mem_avail_lvl_p's exact TOTAL at the claimant's rank (no modelling error, so never a false refusal). (b) cmz_wclaim sizes its first try from mem_avail. Optionally hold the park for one mem_claim_x call rather than one mem_compact call.
findings.verify_note: mem_claim_x loops mem_claim_1 -> mem_compact -> mem_shed_one -> retry (memory.inc:951-989) with no total-size precheck; mem_compact clears [mem_parked] unconditionally at .end, so each compaction may park again when [mem_wpin] is set; cmz_wclaim probes largest window first (compress.inc:3537-3553).

findings.title: The purge floor is lifted by ANY teardown and its task stamp distinguishes no UI-task user
findings.detail: OSAPI_MEM_FLOOR stamps [sch_cur], which is 0 for every package callback, the DOS and the kernel's paste alike. mem_free_rec_x writes MEM_LVL_TOP unconditionally on every instance teardown (a Disk window closing included), and fcp_lend does the same. Concrete failure: a multi-file paste raises the floor to MED so its copy buffer cannot shed MEM_P_FLIST; the user closes any window while an overwrite question is up; under pressure the next entry's copy buffer sheds the list; fcp_lnext finds [fcp_lseg]=0 and ends with DONE - the paste silently stops part-way and reports success. DOS's set/size/post/return/claim sequence can lose its floor the same way.
evidence: kernel/filecp.inc:452-459 paste raises floor to MEM_PG_MED
findings.recommendation: Stamp the floor with inst_caller's instance (DH, 0xFF kernel) as well as the task, and lift it in mem_free_rec_x only when the stamp names the dying instance; or protect the paste by the copy-buffer claim's own rank rather than a machine-wide byte.
findings.verify_note: mmf_osapi_mem_floor stamps AH = [sch_cur] (memory.inc:5848-5852), which is 0 for every UI-task user; mem_free_rec_x and fcp_lend write MEM_LVL_TOP unconditionally (memory.inc:4826, filecp.inc:2348); fcp_lnext reads [fcp_lseg] = 0 as DONE (filecp.inc:536-548). Any instance teardown during a list paste (including a package exiting by itself) lifts the floor.

findings.title: mem_claim_dma_x's head KB->paragraph shift still has the bit-10 carry bug
findings.detail: mov si,cx / mov cl,6 / shl si,cl / jnc: on the 8086 CF is only the last bit out (bit 10). Heads of 1024-2047 KB are refused, but 2048 KB becomes head 0 (no constraint) and 2049 KB a 1KB head, both granted. The claim's AX and mem_regrow's AX already carry cmp ax,1024 guards for exactly this (CODE-REVIEW-TWO-CYCLES #6); the package door passes CX raw.
findings.recommendation: cmp cx, 65 / jae -> SI = 0xFFFF ahead of the shift (mem_claim_1 refuses a head over 0x1000 anyway).
findings.verify_note: memory.inc:860-866: `shl si, cl` with CL = 6 leaves CF = bit 10 only; CX = 2048 gives SI = 0 (no constraint) and 2049 a 64-paragraph head. mmf_osapi_mem_claim_dma passes the package's CX straight in (memory.inc:5254-5266). Low: only a nonsensical head reaches it.

findings.title: The self-region widening in mem_find_own also lets a package FREE or REGROW the region it is running in
findings.detail: mem_find_own accepts DX == BX so OS88_REGION_MOVABLE can name its slot-owned region, but the same fence serves mem_free_x and mem_regrow. OSAPI_MEM_FREE DX=CS frees the executing region; OSAPI_MEM_REGROW DX=CS hitting path 3 copies the region elsewhere and returns with CS still the old, now free, base. Both are the 'one wrong word' accidents the fence exists to stop.
evidence: kernel/loader.inc:1690-1695 the arm is a documented choice
findings.recommendation: Keep mem_find_own's arm (mem_owner_of_x depends on DX = BX matching the first record at DX). If the self-harm is worth closing, refuse a REGION record (MC_OWN < INST_MAX and mem_is_region) in the package doors mmf_osapi_mem_free and osapi_mem_regrow_x only, and reword loader.inc:1690-1695 if the policy changes.
findings.verify_note: Real, but DELIBERATE and documented: loader.inc:1690-1695 says the `cmp dx, bx` arm 'has always let a package name its own region with mov dx, cs and free, regrow or unpin it, which is a package shooting itself and not a thing the kernel undertakes to prevent'. The recommendation as written is wrong: mem_owner_of_x relies on the DX = BX match (memory.inc:5996-6000, 'matches the FIRST live record based at DX whatever it is'), so deleting the arm from mem_find_own breaks it. Severity lowered to low; a fix belongs in the package doors (refuse a region record in mmf_osapi_mem_free/osapi_mem_regrow_x), not in mem_find_own.

findings.title: Nothing bounds the interrupt context any more: blocks an ISR uses move at IF=1 unless they are driver images
findings.detail: SPEC 66.3 bounds ISRs by 'the MC_DMA pin', which no longer exists. Only MC_OWN == MEM_K_DRV moves at IF=0. Yet mem_region_reloc's IVT rows rewrite vectors naming ANY moved block, package regions included, and packages do hook IRQs (DOS chains int 08h with its CS; DOS's region is movable). Today that hook appears to live only inside a bracket where nest/worker pins hold, so the rule is held by coincidence. A tick mid-copy runs the old copy and its data writes are lost once the vector is patched. The same holds for any driver ISR touching a movable data claim (SOUND.DRV is safe only by its per-chunk cli discipline).
evidence: kernel/memory.inc:3474-3483 IVT rows patch any moved block
apps/dos/dos.asm:11445-11446 DOS hooks int 08h with CS
findings.recommendation: Move at IF=0 whenever the block's base appears in any of the 17 mem_rr_ivt segment words (subsumes the driver-image test), and state an ISR author rule in SPEC 66.3.
findings.verify_note: mem_can_move has no MC_DMA test (memory.inc:1987-2000); mem_cp_walk cli's only for MC_OWN == MEM_K_DRV (2973-2976); mem_reloc_call runs mem_region_reloc unconditionally for every move (3869-3871) and its IVT group (mem_rr_ivt, 3473-3483) patches any block named by IRQ0-15 or int 33h. dos_m33_arm hooks int 08h with CS (dos.asm:11431-11446) and DOS's region is MOVABLE (HEAP-CLAIMS.md:329). Whether the hook ever stands outside a pinning bracket is unproven (reviewer's open question 4); latent hazard.

findings.title: O(MEM_MAX^2) walks run with interrupts off (mem_avail, mem_hifit, mem_claim_1)
findings.detail: mem_avail_lvl_p runs the whole compaction model inside pushf/cli: mem_cp_next is a full table scan per step and each live claim calls mem_can_move, which far-calls cw_inst_ptr and inst_seg_parked (an inst_tab walk). By arithmetic ~8-15 ms at IF=0 on a busy 32-record table, against a 7.5 ms serial byte; packages size themselves with it and the Task Manager polls it. mem_hifit (33 x 32) runs under regrow's cli; mem_claim_1's bump-restart is bounded by live claims x table.
findings.recommendation: Measure first: MartyPC cycles across one OSAPI_MEM_AVAIL on a 20-claim heap. If over ~5 ms, guard mem_avail with [sch_lock] instead of cli (its globals are only shared with other tasks). mem-14 removes the n^2.
findings.verify_note: mem_avail_lvl_p's model runs between pushf/cli and popf (memory.inc:4927-5023) and calls mem_cp_next / mem_can_move per step; the 8-15 ms figure is arithmetic, not measured - the recommendation to measure first stands.

findings.title: Regrow path 3 puts every grower at the top, whatever door it came in by
findings.detail: mem_hifit keeps the highest candidate base (the floor or a live claim's end) that fits, i.e. the bottom of the highest free run that fits. Usually that is the middle run, just above the data stack, but when a hole among the ceiling's regions and driver images fits, a bottom-up data claim that grows lands there - the mid-heap split 50.2 was written against - with MC_DMA_HI clear, so the descending pass will not pack it and the ascending pass treats ceiling claims as barriers.
findings.recommendation: Honour the door: lowest fit (or the fit leaving the largest run) for a bottom-up claim, highest only for MC_DMA_HI - one XOR with the mask trick mem_cp_next uses.
findings.verify_note: mem_hifit's candidates are the heap floor and each live claim's END, and it keeps the HIGHEST candidate that fits (memory.inc:1740-1789) - i.e. the BOTTOM of the highest free run that fits. With data bottom-up and regions top-down that is usually the start of the middle run, directly above the data stack, so the grower lands among ceiling claims only when a hole between them fits it. Real but narrower than stated; severity low.

findings.title: mod_drop on a worker can free a module the UI task is executing; and the same missing fact pins every module for life
findings.detail: mod_disarm documents that a drop can run on a worker (inst_task_die -> desk_drop_x) while the UI task far-calls a slot with no lock (DKD_HOVER); its cli prevents a torn slot, not a freed image. If the last widget's own worker dies while the UI task is pre-empted inside dkd_hover for it, the image is freed under the UI task's IP, which does not fault. The missing fact 'is a frame standing in this image' is also why MEM_K_MOD is pinned forever, although a module is named only by kernel words like a driver image.
findings.recommendation: Now: never free a module from a non-UI task; post the drop and service it at ui_task step 0. Rethink: bracket module thunks with wm_nest_pushd/pop so mem_in_nest answers for modules and they can move like driver images.
findings.verify_note: mod_disarm's own note (mod.inc:880-886) says a drop can run on a worker (inst_task_die -> desk_drop_x) while the UI task far-calls a DESK.DRV slot with no lock; desk_drop_x frees through mod_drop (deskmod.inc:116-133) and its banner's 'every other caller is on the UI task' does not cover the worker case. MEM_K_MOD is pinned in mem_can_move (memory.inc:2049-2050).

findings.title: The driver-image IF=0 move's latency note is wrong in both directions
findings.detail: The note says ~50 ms is 'three ticks' and costs 'at most one mouse PACKET'. 50 ms is under one 55 ms tick and the PIC latches one IRQ0, so no tick is lost below ~110 ms; but a 1200-baud mouse delivers ~6-7 bytes into a one-byte 8250 buffer in 50 ms (about two packets), and the SB refill and NIC receive stall too.
findings.recommendation: Correct the text; optionally have the descending pass leave driver images in place unless the plan needs them to move.
findings.verify_note: 18KB at ~25 clocks a word is ~48 ms, under one 55 ms tick, and the PIC holds one IRQ0 pending; the mouse is 1200 baud 7N1 (mouse.inc:617), ~6-7 bytes in 50 ms into a one-byte 8250. Doc fix applied below.

findings.title: Orphaned headers of inlined routines are where this file's documentation rots
findings.detail: About 450 lines of headers describe ten routines that no longer exist as bodies (mem_frameless, mem_busy_seg, mem_cp_mine, mem_cp_both, mem_cp_drop, mem_cp_move, mem_cp_kill, mem_own_drv, mem_dmaok, mem_total_kb). Six of the mismatches in this area are in them, because nobody edits a header with no code under it.
findings.recommendation: Keep three lines at each call site with a SPEC pointer, move the essays to SPEC 66, and have checkdocs refuse an 'INLINE since size pass N' header whose name appears neither as a label nor in SPEC.
findings.verify_note: None of mem_frameless, mem_busy_seg, mem_cp_mine, mem_cp_both, mem_cp_drop, mem_cp_move, mem_cp_kill, mem_own_drv, mem_dmaok, mem_total_kb is a label anywhere in kernel/; their headers remain (e.g. memory.inc:2151, 2173, 2279, 2405, 2595, 5149, 6009), and several of the confirmed doc fixes below are in them.

findings.title: The owner word means four things, and the slot/segment split costs code in five places
findings.detail: MC_OWN is a slot (a region, a built-in's data), a segment (package and driver data, second images), 0xFBxx-0xFExx (caches) or 0xFFxx (kernel tags). Owning the region by slot and the data by segment is why mem_find_own needs the widening (mem-6), mem_rr_tab carries a mem_tab+MC_OWN row, mem_reloc_call classifies three ways, mem_free_rec_x walks twice, and MEM_OWNER_MAX counts region and data apart. Owning everything a package holds by slot (drivers keep segments) deletes four of the five; the cost is CLS_OWN's readers (the Task Manager).
evidence: kernel/memory.inc:5955 mem_own returns ES as owner
findings.recommendation: Record; take it at the flag day with C1 if the Task Manager is touched anyway.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: mem_find_own's widening (memory.inc:4414-4422), the mem_tab+MC_OWN row (3459), mem_reloc_call's three-way split (3880-3906) and mem_free_rec_x's two walks (4831-4841) are as described. Byte estimate unmeasured.

findings.title: Keep mem_tab sorted by base: every walk becomes linear and best fit is free
findings.detail: Each n^2 in the file comes from the table being unordered (mem_cp_next nearest-key scan, mem_claim_1 restart-on-overlap, mem_hifit/mem_runat candidate x table, mem_bigrun). Compaction preserves relative order, so a sorted table stays sorted. Insert/remove is a rep movsw of at most 320 bytes on rare operations. First fit becomes one pass, 50.3.1's unbuilt best fit nearly free, the plan O(n). Blockers: kern_mega pairs selectors with record INDEX (mem_val, MEGA_MSELN); mem_skip and held SI are record pointers; snapshot row order changes.
findings.recommendation: Prototype on kern_big/kern_small behind a knob and measure plan cycles and span; re-key mem_sel by base or keep kern_mega unsorted.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: the restart scan, mem_hifit's candidate x table and mem_cp_next's full scan are as described; kern_mega's MEGA_MSELN == MEM_MAX record-index pairing (memory.inc:126-129) is the stated blocker. Estimate unmeasured.

findings.title: Only the kernel can own a cache: no purgeable class for package claims
findings.detail: The purgeable range is kernel tags only, so a package's rebuildable caches (decoder tables, Sheet's 32KB staging, undo, mix buffers) are walls or freed by hand. Windows' GMEM_DISCARDABLE, Mac purgeable handles and GrowZone, GEOS discardable blocks and AmigaOS low-memory handlers all gave this to applications. MC_DMA bit 13 is free (head <= 0x1000 uses bits 0-12; 14 and 15 are taken). A declared-movable claim could be marked purgeable at a rank by an OSAPI_MEM_P verb, and the shed calls its existing reloc proc with DX=0 ('purged') before freeing.
findings.recommendation: Add the verb and bit; extend mem_pg_cheap/mem_shed_one; document 'DX=0 means purged' in the reloc proc contract. Additive, abilock --update without a bump.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x GMEM_DISCARDABLE + LRU; Mac purgeable handles + GrowZone; GEOS discardable blocks; AmigaOS 3 AddMemHandler
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: MC_DMA_HEAD = 0x3FFF with heads <= 0x1000 (bits 0-12) and bits 14/15 taken (memory.inc:156-164), so bit 13 is free; purgeable ranks are kernel tags only (0xFB..0xFE).

findings.title: No recency inside a rank: the shed takes the first equal-rank record in table order
findings.detail: mem_shed_one keeps the first-seen candidate among equals, and all window raise caches are TRIV, so the cache of the window about to be raised goes as readily as a buried one. Windows discards by LRU and the Mac purges by need. For MEM_P_WSAVE, z-order already is recency.
findings.recommendation: Record; if small-heap redraw cost shows up, shed the deepest window's raise cache first.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x LRU discard list; Mac purge by address/need
findings.verify_note: mem_shed_one's `cmp dl, al / jae .scan` (memory.inc:1421-1422) keeps the first-seen record of the lowest rank.

findings.title: Region movability by package-header bit instead of 72 call sites
findings.detail: Every package carries OS88_REGION_MOVABLE (69 sites in 67 files), 10-19 bytes each plus a far call. A header flag bit read by the loader, with MC_RLOC set to a sentinel meaning 'kernel half only', makes the common case free; mem_reloc_call already runs the kernel's half unconditionally. Old packages keep their call; new ones run pinned on older kernels (safe direction).
evidence: apps/os88api.inc:4829-4836 why a proc is required
findings.recommendation: Add the bit, a sentinel test in mem_reloc_call, and point t_movable at the bit.
findings.bytes_est: +8 .cold kernel; -10..-19 per package image (~-1KB disk tree-wide)
findings.verify_note: The pattern is real; the count is 69 OS88_REGION_MOVABLE lines in 67 files (grep of apps/), not 72. mem_reloc_call does run the kernel's half unconditionally (memory.inc:3869-3871).

findings.title: The KB doors keep regrowing the same carry bug - more evidence for C1
findings.detail: The KB->paragraph conversion has carried the bit-10 carry defect at three doors (claim AX, regrow AX, the DMA head CX of mem-5), each found separately. The paragraph door has no such shift.
findings.recommendation: No new row; cite this as evidence for C1.
findings.verify_note: Evidence is mem-5's and the two guards already in the code; listed as ABI-BREAK-LIST C1.

findings.title: kern_mega osapi_mem_regrow_x's move-down copies the OLD size into the NEW claim
findings.detail: The .move arm sizes the copy from the old KB (shl si, 9) into a conventional claim of the new KB. mega_claimregrowf answers CF = 1 for every regrow of an FH32/FH16/bridge huge block (.hnol -> .nol), shrinks included, so a shrink reaches .move and overruns the new claim; an old size of 128KB+ wraps CX to 0 (nothing copied, the old block freed) and 65-127KB walks a 16-bit offset past the selector's 64KB.
findings.recommendation: Copy min(old, new) KB, and refuse the move (or segment-step it) when that exceeds 64KB.
findings.verify_note: Real and wider than stated. osapi_mem_regrow_x's .move arm copies the OLD KB << 9 words (memory.inc:5440-5468). mega_claimregrowf reaches .nol -> CF = 1 -> .move for ANY regrow of an MX_FH32/MX_FH16/MX_FBRIDGE huge block, shrinks included (mega.inc:12052-12056, 12084), so a shrink overruns the new conventional claim; an old size of 128KB+ makes CX wrap to 0 (nothing copied, block freed), and 65-127KB runs SI/DI past 64KB of the selector. Fix: copy min(old, new) and refuse (or segment-step) past 64KB. kern_mega only and unreleased: low.

findings.title: xm_release_rec carries EMS and NET per-instance teardown
findings.detail: The XMS release issues EMSV_GONE and NETV_GONE driver calls because it has the fourth caller (ld_unreserve); the next per-instance driver resource will be added here or forgotten.
findings.recommendation: One 'instance gone' broadcast over published classes with a GONE verb, called from inst_rel_rec and ld_unreserve.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: xm_release_rec issues DRVC_EMS/EMSV_GONE and DRVC_NET/NETV_GONE (xmem.inc:710-735) because ld_unreserve far-calls it (loader.inc:236).

findings.title: XMS blocks are named by linear address; the 8-block pool cannot be defragmented
findings.detail: A block is its 32-bit base and XM_MAX_BLKS is 8 machine-wide; HIMEM's handles plus lock counts let it move unlocked EMBs. Harmless at today's two consumers.
evidence: kernel/xmem.inc:525-531 xm_alloc returns a linear base
findings.recommendation: Record so the table is not grown without a handle design.
findings.prior_art: HIMEM.SYS XMS handles with lock counts
findings.verify_note: XM_MAX_BLKS equ 8 confirmed at kernel.asm:1948; the rest is a record.

doc_fixes.old_text: the package pool, handed out in KB-granular, segment-aligned blocks to
doc_fixes.new_text: the package pool, handed out in whole granules (MEM_GRAN, 512 bytes - SPEC.md 50.2.1) to
doc_fixes.why: mem_claim_x.gran rounds every claim to MEM_GRAN = 32 paragraphs (memory.inc:933-937); the paragraph doors ask for less than a KB.

doc_fixes.old_text: MC_PARA  equ 2                  ; word: size in paragraphs (KB << 6)
doc_fixes.new_text: MC_PARA  equ 2                  ; word: size in paragraphs, whole MEM_GRAN granules
doc_fixes.why: MC_PARA is AX after mem_claim_x.gran's round to MEM_GRAN (memory.inc:933-937), not KB<<6.

doc_fixes.old_text: CLS_PARA   equ 2                ; word: size in paragraphs (KB << 6)
doc_fixes.new_text: CLS_PARA   equ 2                ; word: size in paragraphs, whole MEM_GRAN granules
doc_fixes.why: The snapshot copies MC_PARA, which is a granule count (memory.inc:933-937).

doc_fixes.old_text:
MC_OWN   equ 4                  ; word: owner - 0..INST_MAX-1 is an instance
                                ; slot; 0xFF00 | tag is the kernel's own
doc_fixes.new_text:
MC_OWN   equ 4                  ; word: owner - 0..INST_MAX-1 an instance
                                ; slot (a package's REGION, a built-in's data);
                                ; otherwise a SEGMENT (a package's or a
                                ; driver's data, SPEC.md 50.2); 0xFBxx..0xFExx
                                ; a purgeable kernel cache (50.6); 0xFF00 | tag
                                ; the kernel's own
doc_fixes.why: mem_own returns the caller's segment as owner (memory.inc:5934-5956); MEM_PG_TRIV..MEM_PG_HIGH = 0xFB..0xFE (memory.inc:344-349).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; Bits 0-14 are the 64KB-page-safe HEAD in
                                ; paragraphs, 0 = no constraint - and
                                ; mem_claim_1 refuses a head over 0x1000, a
                                ; page being 4,096 paragraphs, so the top bit
                                ; is free by that check and not by hope.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; Bits 0-13 are the 64KB-page-safe HEAD in
                                ; paragraphs, 0 = no constraint - and
                                ; mem_claim_1 refuses a head over 0x1000, a
                                ; page being 4,096 paragraphs, so the top two
                                ; bits are free by that check and not by hope.
                                ; (Bit 14 is MC_DISK, below.)
doc_fixes.why: Verifier-found: MC_DISK = 0x4000 and MC_DMA_HEAD = 0x3FFF (memory.inc:156-161), so the head is bits 0-13.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; a smaller) with its region and one spare
doc_fixes.new_text:

                                ; REGION being owned by its instance slot and

doc_fixes.why: mem_claim_1 counts records whose MC_OWN equals BX (memory.inc:1106-1108); a package's data is owned by its segment, its region by its slot.

doc_fixes.new_text:

doc_fixes.why: Driver images are CS-based and do move (memory.inc:2038-2047); MEM_K_MOD is pinned by mem_can_move's own test (2049-2050).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; different lifetimes and only one of them can ever move:
;
;   a data claim can move within its lifetime by being freed and re-claimed;
;   a package region can NEVER move, because its base IS its CS - relocating
;   it would invalidate W_SEG, I_SPTR, every MB_SEG in the menu bar and every
;   claim owner word. SPEC.md 66 compacts the DATA arena and deliberately
;   leaves regions out for exactly this reason.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; different lifetimes and move at different prices:
;
;   a data claim moves whenever its holder declared a proc (SPEC.md 66.2);
;   a package region moves only when no frame stands in it and its worker is
;   restartable (SPEC.md 66.6.1, 66.6.2), and then W_SEG, I_SPTR, every MB_SEG
;   in the menu bar and every claim owner word naming it must be rewritten
;   (mem_region_reloc) - so a CS still costs more to move, and goes high.
doc_fixes.why: mem_can_move's .frameless arm lets a region move (memory.inc:2065-2083) and mem_region_reloc rewrites those words (3229-3253).

doc_fixes.old_text:
;                    reach a task already suspended mid-access, which is what
;                    pins a claim whose owner has a live worker until SPEC.md
;                    66.5's park handshake exists.
;   INTERRUPTS       not bounded by sch_lock at all, so any claim with
;                    MC_DMA != 0 is pinned outright. That is right twice over:
;                    a bus master may be mid-transfer, and the 64KB page rule
;                    is a property of the ADDRESS, so such a block cannot be
;                    relocated even in principle.
doc_fixes.new_text:
;                    reach a task already suspended mid-access, so a claim
;                    whose owner has a live worker moves only once that
;                    worker has PARKED (SPEC.md 66.5, inst_seg_parked).
;   INTERRUPTS       not bounded by sch_lock at all. Only a driver image
;                    moves at IF = 0 (mem_cp_walk, SPEC.md 66.6.3.1), so
;                    its vectors are rewritten before an ISR can run the
;                    old copy; every other block moves with interrupts on.
;                    MC_DMA is a placement constraint the move honours, not
;                    a pin (SPEC.md 66.4.2).
doc_fixes.why: mem_compact parks workers (memory.inc:4095-4106); mem_can_move does not test MC_DMA (1987-2000); only MC_OWN == MEM_K_DRV moves under cli (2973-2976).

doc_fixes.old_text:

doc_fixes.new_text:

doc_fixes.old_text:
; ~50 ms - three ticks - for the largest image in the tree, ETHER's 18KB. That
; is the honest bound and not the typical case. What three lost ticks cost: the
; BIOS clock, and at most one mouse PACKET, which mou_isr resyncs on the
; framing bit rather than corrupting. It cannot land inside a floppy transfer -
doc_fixes.new_text:
; ~50 ms - under one tick - for the largest image in the tree, ETHER's 18KB.
; That is the honest bound and not the typical case. What it costs: no tick,
; the PIC holding one pending; about two serial mouse packets, the 8250 keeping
; one byte of the ~six a 1200-baud mouse sends meanwhile, which mou_isr resyncs
; on the framing bit rather than corrupting; and a sound refill IRQ ~50 ms late.
; It cannot land inside a floppy transfer -
doc_fixes.why: 18KB at ~25 clocks a word is ~48 ms, under a 55 ms tick; a 1200-baud 7N1 mouse sends ~6-7 bytes in 50 ms into a one-byte 8250 (mouse.inc:617).

doc_fixes.old_text:
MC_SEG   0  word  base segment, 0 = free record
MC_PARA  2  word  size in paragraphs (KB << 6)
MC_OWN   4  word  owner: 0..INST_MAX-1 = instance slot;
                  0xFF00 | tag = the kernel's own (MEM_K_SAVE, …);
                  a package's claims carry the SEGMENT it runs in
MC_DMA   6  word  the 64KB-page-safe HEAD in paragraphs, 0 = no constraint
                  (mem_claim_dma, §50.3 — recorded so a claim that MOVES
                  keeps the property it was granted for)
doc_fixes.new_text:
MC_SEG   0  word  base segment, 0 = free record
MC_PARA  2  word  size in paragraphs, a whole number of granules (§50.2.1)
MC_OWN   4  word  owner: 0..INST_MAX-1 = instance slot (a package's REGION,
                  a built-in's data); 0xFBxx..0xFExx = a purgeable kernel
                  cache (§50.6); 0xFF00 | tag = the kernel's own (MEM_K_DRV,
                  …); a package's or driver's data carries the SEGMENT it
                  runs in
MC_DMA   6  word  bits 0-13: the 64KB-page-safe HEAD in paragraphs, 0 = no
                  constraint (mem_claim_dma, §50.3 — recorded so a claim that
                  MOVES keeps the property it was granted for); bit 14
                  MC_DISK, the DISK class (§50.2.1.1); bit 15 MC_DMA_HI, the
                  top-down door
MC_RLOC  8  word  relocation proc, 0 = PINNED (§66.2)
doc_fixes.why: memory.inc:75-125 and 156-161: MC_RLOC at 8, MC_DISK 0x4000, MC_DMA_HI 0x8000, MC_DMA_HEAD 0x3FFF; MEM_K_SAVE no longer exists (memory.inc:166-168).
